categories.description: Internet works but speeds are poor

categories.title: Voice/Phone

basics-start.text: What basic check do you need to walk through?

power-cycle.text: What equipment needs to be power cycled?

power-cycle-ont.title: Power Cycle ONT
steps: Locate the ONT – usually in garage, basement, or utility closet
Unplug the power adapter from the wall (not from the ONT)
Wait 30 seconds
Plug power back in
Wait 2-3 minutes for ONT to fully boot and register
PON light should go solid green when registered
power-cycle-ont.escalation: If ONT won't power on or PON light stays red/off after reboot, check for BBU issues or fiber problems.

power-cycle-router.title: Power Cycle Router/GigaCenter
steps: Unplug the power cord from the back of the router
Wait 30 seconds (lets capacitors fully drain)
Plug power back in
Wait 2-3 minutes for full boot
All status lights should stabilize – Power, Internet, Wi-Fi green
power-cycle-router.escalation: If router won't power on, try different outlet. If still dead, likely hardware failure.

power-cycle-full.title: Full Stack Power Cycle (ONT + Router)
steps: Unplug power from BOTH the ONT and the router
Wait 60 seconds
Plug in ONT FIRST
Wait for ONT PON light to go solid green (2-3 min)
THEN plug in the router
Wait another 2-3 minutes for router to fully boot
Check that Internet light goes green on router
power-cycle-full.escalation: Order matters – ONT must be online before router tries to get WAN IP. If still no internet after full power cycle, move to deeper troubleshooting.

power-cycle-device.title: Power Cycle Customer Device
steps: Have customer fully restart their device (not just sleep/wake)
For computers: Start menu → Restart (not Shut Down)
For phones/tablets: Power off completely, wait 10 sec, power on
For smart TVs/streaming boxes: Unplug from power for 30 sec
After reboot, try reconnecting to Wi-Fi or test internet again
power-cycle-device.escalation: If device still has issues after reboot, check if other devices work to isolate the problem.

physical-connections.text: What connection type are you checking?

check-fiber.title: Check Fiber Connection to ONT
steps: Locate the fiber cable – it's the thin cable with a GREEN SC/APC connector
Check that the green connector is fully seated in the ONT port
Push gently and twist to ensure it's clicked in
NEVER bend fiber cables sharply – minimum 1 inch bend radius
Look for any visible damage, kinks, or crushed sections
Do NOT look into the fiber end – laser light can damage eyes
check-fiber.escalation: If fiber is damaged or connector is broken, do NOT attempt to repair. Dispatch fiber tech.

check-ethernet-ont.title: Check Ethernet from ONT to Router
steps: Locate ethernet cable running from ONT to router WAN port
Check both ends are fully clicked in (should hear/feel click)
Look for damaged or bent pins in the RJ45 connectors
Verify cable goes to WAN/Internet port on router (not LAN)
Try swapping with a known good ethernet cable if available
Check for link lights on both ONT ethernet port and router WAN port
check-ethernet-ont.escalation: If no link lights even with good cable, could be port failure on ONT or router.

check-ethernet-device.title: Check Ethernet from Router to Device
steps: Verify cable is in a LAN port on router (not WAN)
Check cable is fully seated at both router and device
Look for link light on router LAN port
Try a different LAN port on the router
Try a different ethernet cable
Check device's ethernet settings aren't disabled
check-ethernet-device.escalation: If wired connection still fails with different port and cable, test with different device to isolate.

check-phone-port.title: Check Phone/Voice Port Connection
steps: Phone must be plugged into PHONE 1 port (not LAN ports)
Phone ports are typically separate and labeled differently
Use standard phone cable (RJ11) not ethernet (RJ45)
Check cable isn't damaged or pinched
Try a different phone to rule out handset issue
check-phone-port.escalation: If correct port and cable verified but no dial tone, check voice service provisioning.

bbu-check.title: Check for Battery Backup Unit (BBU)
steps: Many ONT installs have a BBU mounted outside near the ONT or on exterior wall
BBU provides backup power during outages but batteries degrade over time
Locate BBU – usually a gray or beige box near fiber entry point
Check BBU status lights – red/amber usually indicates battery issue
If BBU is beeping or showing fault, battery likely needs replacement
Try bypassing BBU: unplug ONT from BBU, plug directly into wall outlet
If ONT works when bypassing BBU, the BBU/battery is the problem
bbu-check.escalation: BBU battery replacement may be customer responsibility depending on provider. Some ISPs will replace, others sell batteries. Confirm policy.

cable-check.text: What type of cable are you verifying?

ethernet-verify.title: Verify Ethernet Cable
steps: Check both RJ45 connectors for bent or pushed-in pins
Ensure plastic clip isn't broken (cable won't stay seated)
Look for cuts, kinks, or crush damage along cable
Cat5e or better recommended – Cat5 may cause issues at gigabit speeds
Cable length should not exceed 100 meters (328 feet)
Avoid running parallel to power cables (causes interference)
Test with a known good cable if available
ethernet-verify.escalation: If cable tests bad, replace. For in-wall runs that can't be replaced, consider MoCA or mesh alternatives.

coax-verify.title: Verify Coax Cable
steps: Check connector is finger-tight on both ends
Look for corrosion on connector threads (green/white buildup)
Verify center pin isn't bent or pushed back
Check for splitters in the line – each split reduces signal
Remove any unnecessary splitters
Look for cable damage – kinks, crush points, or weathering
coax-verify.escalation: Coax signal issues often require signal level meter to diagnose properly.

phone-cable-verify.title: Verify Phone Cable (RJ11)
steps: Phone cables use RJ11 connectors (smaller than ethernet RJ45)
Check connectors aren't cracked or broken
Verify cable clicks securely into phone and router ports
Try a different phone cable – they fail more often than you'd think
Keep phone cables away from power cables and routers (reduces interference)
phone-cable-verify.escalation: If verified cable and still no dial tone, move to voice service troubleshooting.

check-lights.text: What's the status of the PON/Link light on the ONT or GigaCenter?
check-lights.help: This is usually the second light from the top. It indicates fiber connectivity.

power-issue.title: Power Issue
steps: Check if power cable is connected securely
Verify outlet has power (test with another device)
Try a different outlet
Check for tripped breaker or GFI outlet
If using power strip, bypass and plug directly to wall
power-issue.escalation: If power confirmed at outlet but unit won't power on, likely hardware failure. Schedule tech dispatch.

pon-no-signal.title: No Fiber Signal Detected
steps: Check fiber cable connection at ONT (green SC/APC connector)
Ensure connector is fully seated – push and twist
Inspect fiber for visible damage or tight bends
Check Calix Cloud for OLT port status
pon-no-signal.escalation: If fiber connected properly and no visible damage, likely fiber path issue. Create ticket for fiber team.

pon-los.title: Loss of Signal (LOS)
steps: Fiber signal not reaching ONT
Check fiber connection – reseat green connector
Inspect visible fiber run for damage
Check Calix Cloud Rx power if available
pon-los.escalation: LOS typically indicates fiber break or OLT issue. Check for area outages. If isolated, dispatch fiber tech.

pon-registering.title: ONT Attempting to Register
steps: ONT sees signal but can't complete registration
Wait 2-3 minutes for registration to complete
If persists, check provisioning in Calix Cloud
Verify ONT serial number matches account
Try rebooting ONT (unplug power 30 sec)
pon-registering.escalation: If still blinking after reboot and provisioning verified, may be OLT issue or ONT fault.

check-internet-led.text: Good – PON link is up. What's the Internet/WAN light showing?

dhcp-failure.title: DHCP/WAN IP Failure
steps: ONT link is good but router not getting WAN IP
Check service profile in Calix Cloud
Verify VLAN configuration is correct
Check account status – is billing active?
Reboot router to retry DHCP
dhcp-failure.escalation: If provisioning looks correct and reboot doesn't help, escalate to provisioning team.

internet-led-good.text: Internet light is green. Is this affecting all devices or just one?

all-devices-down.title: All Devices Down Despite Good LEDs
steps: Router appears online but no traffic passing
Check Calix Cloud – verify management connectivity
Try pinging router gateway (usually 192.168.1.1)
Full power cycle: unplug ONT and router, wait 60 sec, plug ONT first, wait for green lights, then router
all-devices-down.escalation: If power cycle doesn't resolve, check for firmware issues or escalate for deeper diagnostics.

single-device.title: Single Device Issue
steps: Issue is isolated to one device – not network-wide
Restart the affected device
Forget network and reconnect with password
Check device isn't blocked in parental controls
Try connecting device to different band (2.4 vs 5GHz)
single-device.escalation: If device still can't connect after troubleshooting, issue is with the device itself.

wifi-only-down.text: Only Wi-Fi devices affected. Can wired devices connect?

wifi-disabled.title: Wi-Fi Issue – Check Configuration
steps: Check if Wi-Fi LED is on
Verify Wi-Fi isn't disabled in CommandIQ or Calix Cloud
Check if SSID is broadcasting (can devices see network?)
Reboot router to reset Wi-Fi radios
wifi-disabled.escalation: If Wi-Fi still not working after reboot and settings verified, may need firmware update or replacement.

test-type.text: Is the slowness on Wi-Fi, wired, or both?

wifi-slow.text: What speeds are they seeing on Wi-Fi vs their plan speed?
wifi-slow.help: Have them run speedtest.net on Wi-Fi

wifi-very-slow.text: What band is their device connected to?
wifi-very-slow.help: Check in Wi-Fi settings or CommandIQ

move-to-5ghz.title: Move Device to 5GHz Band
steps: 2.4GHz is limited to ~50-100Mbps actual throughput
Have customer connect to 5GHz network if available
If separate SSIDs, connect to the 5G one
If same SSID, forget network and reconnect closer to router
Check Wi-Fi analytics for band steering recommendations
move-to-5ghz.escalation: If 5GHz not reaching device, may need mesh satellite for coverage.

check-wifi-interference.title: Check Wi-Fi Interference
steps: Check Calix Cloud Wi-Fi analytics for interference
Look for neighboring networks on same channel
Enable auto channel selection if not already
Check router placement – move away from metal, appliances
Consider channel width – 40MHz vs 80MHz
check-wifi-interference.escalation: If interference persists after optimization, customer may be in high-density Wi-Fi area. Consider mesh or wired backhaul.

wifi-moderate-slow.title: Wi-Fi Performance Within Normal Range
steps: 50-80% of plan speed on Wi-Fi is generally acceptable
Wi-Fi overhead typically reduces speeds by 20-40%
Check distance from router
Verify no bandwidth-heavy activities (large downloads, streaming on multiple devices)
wifi-moderate-slow.escalation: Set expectations. For full speeds, recommend wired connection or consider upgrading to Wi-Fi 6 equipment.

wifi-acceptable.title: Wi-Fi Performance is Good
steps: Over 80% of plan speed on Wi-Fi is excellent
This is expected performance
If customer still unhappy, discuss plan upgrade options
wifi-acceptable.escalation: No technical issue. May be expectation management or need for faster plan.

wired-slow.text: What speeds on wired? What's the plan speed?

options.label: Close to plan but expecting more

check-provisioning.title: Check Provisioning and ONT Levels
steps: Verify speed tier in Calix Cloud matches account
Check Rx power levels – poor signal affects throughput
Verify customer is testing with Gigabit-capable device
Check Ethernet cable quality (Cat5e or better needed)
Run speed test from Calix Cloud if available
check-provisioning.escalation: If provisioning correct and levels good, may need deeper network diagnostics.

plan-expectation.title: Plan Speed Expectations
steps: Confirm what plan speed they're paying for
Speeds are 'up to' not guaranteed
Check if they're getting at least 80% of plan on wired
Verify overhead on connection type
plan-expectation.escalation: No technical issue if hitting close to plan speed. Discuss upgrade if customer needs more.

both-slow.title: Overall Connection Slow
steps: Issue likely at ONT or network level, not Wi-Fi
Check Rx power levels in Calix Cloud
Verify service profile and speed tier
Check for network congestion at OLT level
Reboot ONT and router
both-slow.escalation: If levels and provisioning good, escalate to network team for path analysis.

drop-frequency.text: How often is the connection dropping?

frequent-drops.text: Is it all devices or specific devices dropping?

check-ont-logs.title: Check ONT Event Logs
steps: Pull event logs from Calix Cloud
Look for LOS, LOF, or dying gasp events
Check Rx power history for fluctuations
Look for times matching customer's reported drops
check-ont-logs.escalation: If logs show optical events, fiber path issue. If dying gasp, power issue at location.

roaming-issue.title: Possible Roaming Issue
steps: If mesh setup, devices may be bouncing between units
Check roaming settings in Calix Cloud
Enable/adjust band steering
Consider reducing satellite count if oversaturated
Check backhaul strength between units
roaming-issue.escalation: If roaming settings don't help, may need to adjust mesh topology or add wired backhaul.

wifi-drops.title: Wi-Fi Specific Drops
steps: Check Wi-Fi analytics for interference spikes
Look for DFS events (radar detection on 5GHz)
Check for overheating – is unit hot?
Reduce channel width if congested area
Reboot router to reset Wi-Fi radios
wifi-drops.escalation: If DFS events frequent, move to non-DFS channels. If overheating, check ventilation or replace unit.

occasional-drops.title: Occasional Drops – Monitor
steps: Document times when drops occur
Check if correlates with high-usage periods
Review event logs for that timeframe
Ensure firmware is up to date
occasional-drops.escalation: If pattern emerges (same time daily), may indicate scheduled processes or external interference.

check-pattern.text: Any correlation with weather, time of day, or activities?

weather-drops.title: Weather-Related Drops
steps: Drops during rain/wind suggest physical plant issue
Check for aerial fiber or exposed connections
Look for water intrusion at splice points
May need fiber team site visit
weather-drops.escalation: Weather-correlated issues typically require physical inspection and repair. Create dispatch ticket.

time-pattern.title: Time-Based Pattern
steps: Could be network congestion at peak hours
Check for scheduled tasks (backups, updates)
Review network-wide performance at those times
Consider if neighbor on same PON has heavy usage
time-pattern.escalation: If congestion issue, may need network capacity review.

random-drops.title: Random Intermittent Issues
steps: Check all connections – reseat fiber and Ethernet
Review Rx power over time for micro-fluctuations
Check for firmware update availability
Consider swap of ONT/router to rule out hardware
random-drops.escalation: Intermittent issues are hardest to diagnose. If troubleshooting doesn't reveal cause, schedule tech for swap-out.

cant-see-network.title: Network Not Visible
steps: Check Wi-Fi LED on router – is it on?
Verify SSID broadcast is enabled in settings
Check if Wi-Fi is disabled in CommandIQ/Calix Cloud
Try scanning from different device
Reboot router
cant-see-network.escalation: If Wi-Fi appears disabled and can't enable, may be hardware or firmware issue.

wont-connect.text: What error do they get when trying to connect?

password-issue.title: Password Verification
steps: Look up Wi-Fi password in CommandIQ or Calix Cloud
Passwords are case-sensitive
Have customer forget network and re-enter password
Check for special characters being entered incorrectly
Can reset password from Calix Cloud if needed
password-issue.escalation: If password correct and still failing, check for MAC filtering or device limits.

dhcp-device.title: Device Can't Get IP Address
steps: Router DHCP may be exhausted
Check connected device count in Calix Cloud
Expand DHCP pool if needed
Check if device has static IP conflict
Restart device and try again
dhcp-device.escalation: If DHCP pool not exhausted, may be device compatibility issue.

timeout-issue.title: Connection Timeout
steps: Device may be too far from router
Move closer and try again
Check if device is blacklisted/blocked
Try connecting to 2.4GHz (better range)
Reboot both router and device
timeout-issue.escalation: If still timing out at close range, may be device or router radio issue.

connected-no-internet.title: Connected to Wi-Fi but No Internet
steps: Check if other Wi-Fi devices have internet
Verify this specific device works on other networks
Check for captive portal or authentication needed
Flush DNS on device (ipconfig /flushdns on Windows)
Check parental controls aren't blocking device
connected-no-internet.escalation: If other devices work fine, issue is with this specific device.

dead-zone.title: Dead Zone in Specific Area
steps: Check router placement – should be central
Identify obstacles (thick walls, metal, appliances)
Consider adding mesh satellite in or near dead zone
Run coverage map if available in Calix Cloud
dead-zone.escalation: Recommend mesh satellite for persistent dead zones. Check for existing mesh and placement.

general-weak.title: Generally Weak Coverage
steps: Check router placement – not in basement/closet
Elevate router if on floor
Check antenna orientation if external antennas
Consider mesh system for larger homes
Verify firmware is current
general-weak.escalation: May need mesh upgrade for adequate coverage in larger homes.

outdoor-coverage.title: Outdoor/Detached Coverage
steps: Standard indoor routers aren't designed for outdoor coverage
Exterior walls significantly reduce signal
Options: outdoor AP, mesh satellite in closest indoor spot, or wired connection to detached building
outdoor-coverage.escalation: Outdoor coverage typically requires additional equipment or wired backhaul.

no-dial-tone.text: Is phone connected to Phone 1 port on router?

wrong-port.title: Move Phone to Correct Port
steps: Phone should be in Phone 1 port (not LAN ports)
Phone 1 port is typically marked differently
Move phone cable to Phone 1
Wait 30 seconds, pick up and check for dial tone
wrong-port.escalation: If still no dial tone after moving to correct port, proceed to check voice service.

check-port.title: Verify Phone Port
steps: Look at back of GigaCenter/ONT
Phone ports are separate from LAN ports
Usually labeled 'Phone 1' or 'Tel 1'
Move phone to Phone 1 if not already there
check-port.escalation: Continue to voice service check after verifying port.

check-voice-service.title: Check Voice Service Provisioning
steps: Verify voice service is active on account
Check voice line status in Calix Cloud
Look for SIP registration status
Try rebooting GigaCenter to re-register SIP
Verify phone number is provisioned correctly
check-voice-service.escalation: If voice service shows active but no dial tone, may be SIP server or ATA issue. Escalate to voice team.

calls-dropping.title: Calls Dropping
steps: Check internet stability – drops affect voice
Review QoS settings – voice should be prioritized
Check for bandwidth saturation during calls
Verify SIP settings are correct
Check for router overheating
calls-dropping.escalation: If internet stable but calls drop, may be SIP/codec issue. Escalate to voice team.

poor-quality.title: Poor Call Quality
steps: Check for jitter and packet loss on connection
Verify QoS is enabled and prioritizing voice
Check bandwidth – is customer saturating connection?
Try reducing codec from G.711 to G.729 if applicable
Verify no SIP ALG issues (should usually be disabled)
poor-quality.escalation: If connection quality good but voice bad, may be codec or SIP server issue.

one-way-audio.title: One-Way Audio
steps: Usually caused by NAT or SIP ALG issues
Check if SIP ALG is enabled – try disabling it
Verify RTP ports aren't being blocked
Check if customer has double-NAT situation
Reboot router to clear NAT tables
one-way-audio.escalation: One-way audio is typically network/NAT related. May need advanced SIP configuration.

cant-receive.title: Cannot Receive Calls
steps: Verify phone number is ported/active
Check call forwarding isn't enabled accidentally
Test calling from different number/phone
Check Do Not Disturb settings if applicable
Verify SIP registration is active
cant-receive.escalation: If can make but not receive, usually SIP registration or number routing issue.
